line: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 Bg4 Bc4
teaches: When a natural-looking move lets the opponent trade into your centre with tempo, prefer the developing move whose consequences you can see to the end — a sound piece on a good square beats a sharper move whose compensation you would be hunting for afterwards.
explains: The bishop takes the f7 diagonal instead of the quiet pawn move — which would have allowed a trade on f3 followed by a capture in the centre. Not every position needs the theoretically best try: development is finished on c4, a square whose value does not depend on a calculation, eyeing f7 and holding d5.
